new.analysis:
Aug 24 – 30 came in at 27 miles against 36 planned. Most of the gap came from two sessions cut short and one missed run.

| Session | Planned | Done |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tue easy | 6 mi | 6.00 mi |
| Wed threshold | 8 mi | 6.03 mi, two of three reps |
| Thu easy | 5 mi | missed |
| Sat easy | 4 mi | 4.00 mi |
| Sun long | 13 mi | 11.00 mi, cut short |

Heat explains most of the heart-rate picture. Easy runs averaged 151 bpm at 10:28/mi, against 138 bpm at 9:50/mi three weeks ago, and the long run drifted from 150 to 161. Those paces ran at about 139 bpm in cooler weeks, so heat and fatigue are the likely cause, not lost fitness.

Sleep and stress are making the heat harder to handle. You averaged 5.5 hours, feel drained, and the AC is out until next week. A load like that blunts recovery, so this plan trims intensity rather than adding volume to catch up.

The quality session stays, but shorter. Threshold work is what the build phase needs, and dropping it would cost more fitness than it saves. Two reps with a heart-rate ceiling keep the stimulus without the overheated effort you saw on Wednesday.

Making up the missed miles would add about seven miles on tired legs eight weeks out, which is the wrong trade. The plan still rebuilds above the 27 miles you ran, and the long run returns to the 11 miles you finished.

Marathon-pace segments can wait. They add real fatigue, so they belong in long runs once sleep improves and the heat drops, likely in the next two to three weeks. Until then, flatter routes on the long run are a sensible precaution after the mid-August knee flare.
